html:
The Mongol-led dynasty that ruled China from 1271 to 1368. It was founded by Kublai Khan and was the first dynasty from outside the Han Chinese to rule all of China.

The Mongols had held northern China since they destroyed the Jin in 1234. Kublai proclaimed the Great Yuan in 1271 in the Chinese style, and finished off the Song in 1279. His capital, Khanbaliq, became today's Beijing. The Yuan was one of four khanates the Mongol Empire split into, but its rulers kept the title of Great Khan.

How it ruled:

  • People were ranked by origin: Mongols first, then Central Asians and other foreigners, then northern Chinese, and southern Chinese last.
  • The civil service exams were stopped for decades and brought back only in 1315, on a small scale.
  • Paper money was the main currency, and the Grand Canal was cut straight to the capital.

Under Mongol rule the roads across Asia were open. Travellers such as Marco Polo came east, and Rabban Bar Sauma went west. Persian cobalt gave China its blue and white porcelain. Theatre and popular drama flourished.

Failed invasions of Japan and Southeast Asia drained the treasury. In the 14th century, printing too much paper money, Yellow River floods, famine and plague hit hard. The Red Turban rebels rose in the 1350s, and one of their leaders, Zhu Yuanzhang, took Beijing in 1368 and founded the Ming. The Mongol court fled back to the steppe, where it carried on as the Northern Yuan.
sum: The Mongol-led dynasty that ruled China from 1271 to 1368. It was founded by Kublai Khan and was the first dynasty from outside the Han Chinese to rule all of China.
